concepts.why: Biblical-theological / academic: the name is 'Other gods and idols', but Jer 2:13 as a single verse says only 'they have forsaken Me, the fountain of living water' and 'dug their own cisterns'; it names no god or idol (that is Jer 2:11, 'exchanged their Glory for worthless idols'). The cisterns-as-idols reading is an inference. Either drop Jer 2:13 or widen it to Jeremiah 2:11-13 so the passage itself says 'gods' and 'idols'. Dropping is simpler, since Jer 1:16 and Judg 10:13 already carry 'forsaken Me and served other gods'.

Academic / Jewish / Orthodox / Reformed: the name is a question about every 'one born of woman', but Ps 58:3 says only that 'the wicked are estranged from the womb', which is about a class of people, not the human condition at birth. It makes the concept say more than that passage. Keep Job 14:4, 15:14, 25:4 and Ps 51:5 (the one first-person verse that speaks of conception). Note for the owner, not a change: Job 15:14 and 25:4 are speeches of Eliphaz and Bildad, whom God says have not spoken rightly (Job 42:7). The page quotes them plainly and gives no gloss, so the grouping is acceptable, but nothing should be added that presents them as the book's own verdict.

Academic (original arbitrates): 'delivered us into the hand of our iniquity' is the Berean's reading of a difficult Hebrew verb. Other translations take it from 'melt' or 'consume' (for example 'made us melt in the hand of our iniquity'). The MACULA lemma should be checked. If it is the 'melt' root, this verse does not say God gave them over and should go from this concept. The verse is already used in 'I will hide My face', where its 'hidden Your face from us' is plain, so nothing is lost by dropping it here. (Rom 1:26 also carries a sentence on sexual relations beyond 'gave them over'. It is the text's own and part of the Rom 1:24/26/28 triple, so it is kept.)

concepts.name: You were dead
concepts.why: Name against passages: 'in your trespasses' is said only by Eph 2:1, Eph 2:5 and Col 2:13. Luke 15:24 ('dead and is alive again'), 1 John 3:14 ('remains in death') and Rev 3:1 ('you are dead') say 'dead' of living people without naming trespasses, so half the passages say less than the name. 'You were dead' is Paul's word (Eph 2:1) and the plain common ground; 'Dead while alive' would also be a plain label. The name 'Dead in your trespasses' also reads as the specific doctrinal gloss (death as a condition of sin) that Reformed, Wesleyan and Orthodox readers take differently.

secondary_or_links: Concept 36 (the closing hope): accepted. It is last, it is made of the theme's own verses for sin (Isa 40:2, Rom 5:20), exile (Deut 30:3-4, Ezek 36:24) and death (Isa 25:8, Ezek 37:12, 1 Cor 15:54-55), and concept 35 (the lament with no answer) stands directly before it, so nothing dark is softened. Rom 5:20's name over Old Testament verses only places them together and does not say one fulfils the other, since each passage speaks for itself.

Concept 2: Rev 12:9 kept on the drafter's reasoning. The verse itself says 'that ancient serpent' and the name makes no claim about who the Genesis serpent is. Nothing in the concept or its notes should add one.

Secondary lines and links: no change. All notes and quoted passages checked against the packet text are exact, and none of the secondary lines claims fulfilment or an interpretation. 'Law/Wisdom' and 'Wisdom Literature' are both kept, as the drafter says they are distinct themes.
